title: Forced Draft Fan
model_title: Forced Draft (FD) Fan with Inlet Silencer & Inlet Guide Vanes

introduction.definition: A forced draft (FD) fan pushes combustion air into a boiler through the air heater and windbox to the burners. It handles clean ambient air; inlet guide vanes (or blade pitch / speed) control the airflow to match the fuel.
key_points: IGVs save energy compared with dampers

introduction.summary: A forced draft (FD) fan pushes ambient combustion air into a boiler through the air heater and windbox to the burners. It handles clean, cold air, so it can run at high efficiency; inlet guide vanes or blade pitch/speed control set the airflow to match the fuel.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Provide good inlet conditions: straight duct or bellmouth; avoid elbows close to the inlet (system effect).
Fit flexible connections at inlet and outlet.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

periodic.task: Clean impeller and housing; check inlet cone gap.

lubrication: Grease or oil bath for the plummer-block bearings; motor bearings per maker.

causes: Dust build-up or erosion on blades

video_tutorials.title: Forced Draft Fan — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Forced Draft Fan.
A forced draft (FD) fan pushes combustion air into a boiler through the air heater and windbox to the burners.
It handles clean ambient air; inlet guide vanes (or blade pitch / speed) control the airflow to match the fuel.
Typical applications include boilers (combustion air); furnaces and kilns; fluidised bed boilers (with PA fans); large burner systems.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Scroll (Volute) Housing with Outlet, Impeller (12 backward-curved aerofoil blades), Hub & Shaft, Inlet Cone (Venturi), Inlet Silencer (absorptive, with acoustic pod).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Forced Draft Fan — Operation

script.narration: How the Forced Draft Fan works.
Air enters through the inlet silencer.
Inlet guide vanes pre-swirl the air to reduce flow and power at part load.
The spinning blades throw the air outward, adding velocity and pressure.
The scroll housing collects the air; its widening passage slows it and turns velocity into pressure.
Bearings and the coupled motor drive the shaft.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Forced Draft Fan — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Forced Draft Fan.
Check bearing temperature and vibration.
Stroke-test IGV actuator.
Clean impeller and housing; check inlet cone gap.
Check coupling alignment.
Inspect impeller for erosion/cracks; re-balance.
Replace bearings.
Watch for vibration from imbalance: rising 1× running-speed vibration. Common cause: dust build-up or erosion on blades.
Watch for bearing overheating: high bearing temperature. Common cause: lack/excess of grease, misalignment.
Watch for igv linkage seizure: airflow not controllable. Common cause: corrosion, lack of lubrication.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
